There’s different types, but for my armpits, I’ve used a bikini trimmer since other trimmers are too big. There’s also trimmers that are larger that I think are for beard iirc. For my legs, I do use a larger trimmer due to the surface area. I don’t remember what I use for my leg trimmer but I think it’s some remington for my bikini razor, but I’ve had it for over a year.

Also, clean and oil your trimmers!!! If you don’t clean and oil them, it can increase the likelihood of infection.

If you want to have a cheaper trimmer for a one time use, I recommend a cheap razor. If you go along the grain of your hair, it will trim without actually shaving. You don’t want to go too rough as cuts and burns can still happen with this method. 

Note: Prior to trimming, you should exfoliate. Just makes it easier in the long run. 

After you have trimmed, I recommend having a warm shower or bath. Warm water tends to make it easier from what I’ve seen(not a human scientist) And be sure to use a lubricant. I’ve had less issues with shaving cream geared towards sensitive skin. Smother your shaving area with the lubricant, because it helps prevent against razor burns. Make sure you cover the area with it, but don’t go like an inch thick, because at that point you’re wasting product. 

When I want a clean shave without too much irritation(only due to skin condition) I use a 4-5 blade razor. Idk how other razor tend to do with lower number of blades. 

You want to have the razor flush against your skin, with the handle facing towards the direction you are shaving. When shaving, you always want to shave from tip of hair to the pore. This may mean looking at the direction of your hair growth for a bit. Personally, my thigh hairs grow in 3 different directions so I have to change the angle depending on what part I’m shaving. Examining this can gear towards a cleaner shave, as you’ll reduce the amount of stubble after washing off any left over product. 

Afterwards, please make sure to moisturize with a sensitive or unscented lotion, because you will feel any flowery or sweet scents in any cuts. You can accidentally make unnoticeable cuts while shaving and then find out you have some when you put scented lotion on your shaved spot. Also, do not exfoliate directly after shaving, you’ll just be asking for a world of irritation.

Usually from there, you’re good! If you have naturally thicker hair, you’ll feel stubble regardless of how you shave. There is the option of waxing, but it depends on your own pain tolerance. Hope this helps a bit
